payload.claim: `_spec_path_pattern` guesses the spec file's path as `.saffron/specs/{spec_id}-*.md` and the docstring (line 259) asserts this 'matches the one file `SA-0005` could ever name, and nothing else' — but nothing in the schema or `discover_specs` (saffron/intake.py:196, which just globs `*.md` and reads `id` from frontmatter) ties a spec file's name to its `id`. `CellSpec` never carries the actual discovered path (the docstring itself admits this at line 257), so this is a guessed convention, not a derived fact. Every spec in this repo happens to follow `<id>-<slug>.md`, so the tests (including the SA-0005 fixture test) can't expose the gap, but a target repo whose spec files don't follow that naming (fully legal per the schema) would get a `final_touches` entry that never matches the real spec path, and the ratification's first commit would fail its own `scope` gate — exactly the failure this code (session.py:862-864, mirroring DESIGN.md's bug-ratification writeback rule) exists to prevent.
